---
title: "Research"
---

My research focuses on how linguistic structures emerge, change, and persist through time. I combine historical and comparative linguistics with quantitative modelling, phylogenetic methods, and cross-linguistic typology.

## Syntax and linguistic evolution

A central strand of my work concerns the evolution of syntactic hierarchy, especially in clause-linkage constructions. I am interested in how relations between clauses vary across languages, how those structures evolve, and how syntactic organization interacts with semantics.

My doctoral dissertation, *Syntactic Hierarchy in Linguistic Evolution: A Phylogenetic View of Clause-Linkage*, developed a phylogenetic perspective on these questions.

## Comparative typology and phylogenetics

I use Bayesian phylogenetic inference and phylogenetic comparative methods to investigate historical dependencies in cross-linguistic data. This work addresses questions that are difficult to answer from synchronic typological distributions alone, because related languages are not statistically independent observations.

Methodologically, my work includes:

- Bayesian phylogenetic inference
- phylogenetic comparative methods
- Bayesian hierarchical modelling
- Gaussian processes
- comparative typology
- corpus-based quantitative analysis

## Historical and Semitic linguistics

My broader research background includes Semitic languages, historical phonology, Hebrew and Aramaic varieties, and transcription systems. I have worked on Biblical Hebrew rhotics, Mandaic transcription and annotation, and comparative resources for Semitic transcription and transliteration.

## Computational modelling

I also work with computational approaches to historical linguistics and language evolution. Earlier work included neural proto-language reconstruction, while more recent work combines computational modelling with typological and phylogenetic data.

## Technical methods

I work primarily with **R**, **Python**, and **SQL**, with statistical modelling in **Stan** and phylogenetic analysis in **BEAST2**. My research workflow uses Git, Linux, Slurm/HPC, Quarto, R Markdown, Pandoc, and LaTeX.
